 1                    I.      INTRODUCTION AND QUALIFICATIONS

 2   Q1.   PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME, BUSINESS ADDRESS.

 3   A.    My name is Manuel Carrasco. My business address is 100 North Stanton Street,

 4         El Paso, Texas, 79901.

 5

 6   Q2.   ON WHOSE BEHALF ARE YOU SUBMITTING THIS TESTIMONY

 7   A.    I am filing this testimony on behalf of El Paso Electric Company (“EPE” or “the

 8         Company”).

 9

10   Q3.   HAVE YOU PREVIOUSLY SUBMITTED TESTIMONY IN THIS

11         PROCEEDING?

12   A.    Yes. I submitted Direct Testimony in this proceeding on March 27, 2026.

13

14             II.     PURPOSE OF SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT TESTIMONY

15   Q4.   WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT

16         TESTIMONY?

17   A.    The purpose of my Supplemental Direct Testimony is to respond to Pre-Hearing

18         Bench Request Paragraphs 9.b.i, 9.b.ii, 9.f, 9.g, 9.h, and 9.n.

19

 3   Q5.   WHAT HAS THE COMMISSION REQUESTED IN PARAGRAPHS 9.b.i

 4         AND 9.b.ii OF THE PRE-HEARING BENCH REQUEST?

 5   A.    Paragraphs 9.b.i and 9.b.ii of the Pre-Hearing Bench Request request that EPE

 6         provide for (a) each class of service, (b) separately for the summer and non-summer

 7         months, and (c) for various levels of use, the following:

 8         •      Paragraph 9.b.i “The monthly bill under current rates stating separately the

 9                customer charge, usage charge, any demand charge, the Fuel and Purchased

10                Power Cost Adjustment Clause (FPPCAC) charge, any other separate charges

11                (such as the renewable energy and energy efficiency rider charges) but

12                excluding taxes and surcharges and the total bill.”

13         •      Paragraph 9.b.ii “The monthly bill under proposed rates separately stating the

14                customer charge, usage charge, any demand charge, the FPPCAC charge, any

15                other separate charges (such as the renewable energy and energy efficiency

16                rider charges) but excluding taxes and surcharges and the total bill.”

17

18   Q6.   IN RESPONSE TO PARAGRAPH 9.b.i, WHAT IS THE MONTHLY BILL

19         UNDER CURRENT RATES (SEPARATELY STATING THE CUSTOMER

20         CHARGE, USAGE CHARGE, ANY DEMAND CHARGE, THE FPPCAC

 2        TAXES AND SURCHARGES AND THE TOTAL BILL) FOR (a) EACH

4         SUMMER MONTHS, AND (c) FOR VARIOUS LEVELS OF USE.

5    A.   The requested monthly bill information under current rates is provided in Exhibit

 6        MC-02 (Bill Impacts), which was filed with my Direct Testimony. Exhibit MC-02

 7        includes detailed bill calculation tables for each rate class (Tabs A through F) as

 8        follows:

 9           •   Tab A. Bills Default Ph 1 includes the bill impact analysis comparing the

10               current and proposed rates for the proposed Phase 1 of the default or

11               “standard” rates;

12           •   Tab B. Bills Optional Ph 1 includes the bill impact analysis comparing the

13               current and proposed rates for the proposed Phase 1 of the optional Time-

14               of-Day rates;

15           •   Tab C. Bills Default Ph 2 includes the bill impact analysis comparing the

16               current and proposed rates for the proposed Phase 2 of the default or

17               “standard” rates;

18           •   Tab D. Bills Optional Ph 2 includes the bill impact analysis comparing the

19               current and proposed rates for the proposed Phase 2 of the optional Time-

20               of-Day rates;

19   (a) For each class of service,

20   (b) Separately for annual average, summer, and non-summer billing periods, and

10   Q8.   WHAT HAS THE COMMISSION REQUESTED IN PARAGRAPH 9.f OF

11         THE PRE-HEARING BENCH REQUEST?

12   A.    Paragraph 9.f of the Pre-Hearing Bench Request requests “…the base cost of fuel

13         (per kWh) incorporated into EPE’s existing rates.”

14

15   Q9.   IN RESPONSE TO PARAGRAPH 9.f, WHAT IS THE BASE COST OF

16         FUEL (PER kWh) INCORPORATED INTO EPE’S EXISTING RATES?

17   A.    None. Pursuant to the Commission’s Final Order in Case No. 15-00127-UT, the

18         Company was required to remove all fuel and purchased power costs from base

19         rates and bill such costs through the Fuel and Purchased Power Cost Adjustment

20         Clause (“FPPCAC”).


                                               6
                              EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY
                         SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
                                 MANUEL CARRASCO


 1   Q10. WHAT HAS THE COMMISSION REQUESTED IN PARAGRAPH 9.g OF

 2        THE PRE-HEARING BENCH REQUEST?

 3   A.   Paragraph 9.g of the Pre-Hearing Bench Request requests “…the base cost of fuel

 4        incorporated into EPE’s proposed rates? Provide the dollar cost of fuel for the test

 5        year and the billing units expressed in kWh used to determine the base cost of fuel.”

 6

 7   Q11. IN RESPONSE TO PARAGRAPH 9.g, WHAT IS THE BASE COST OF

 8        FUEL INCORPORATED INTO EPE’S PROPOSED RATES? PROVIDE

 9        THE DOLLAR COST OF FUEL FOR THE TEST YEAR AND THE

10        BILLING UNITS EXPRESSED IN kWh USED TO DETERMINE BASE

11        COST OF FUEL.

12   A.   None. Please see EPE’s response to paragraph 9.f above.

13

14   Q12. WHAT HAS THE COMMISSION REQUESTED IN PARAGRAPH 9.h OF

15        THE PRE-HEARING BENCH REQUEST?

16   A.   Paragraph 9.h of the Pre-Hearing Bench Request requests “If EPE were to collect

17        all of its fuel costs through base rates, what would be the base cost of fuel

18        incorporated into the new rates proposed to take effect on January 1, 2027, and

19        subsequently on October 1, 2027 (or whenever the proposed rates become

20        effective)?”


                                                7
                             EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY
                        SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
                                MANUEL CARRASCO


 1   Q13. IN RESPONSE TO PARAGRAPH 9.h, PROVIDE THE BASE COST OF

 2        FUEL INCORPORATED INTO THE NEW RATES PROPOSED TO TAKE

 3        EFFECT ON JANUARY 1, 2027, AND SUBSEQUENTLY ON OCTOBER 1,

 4        2027, IF EPE WERE TO COLLECT ALL ITS FUEL COSTS THROUGH

 5        BASE RATES.

 6   A.   EPE is not proposing to incorporate fuel costs into any of the rates proposed in this

7         proceeding. For illustrative purposes only, Exhibit MC-1S at lines 19 through 23

8         column (d) provides the “base cost of fuel” that could be incorporated into base

 9        rates, which is about one cent per kWh. Because the Final Order in Case No. 15-

10        00127-UT required EPE to remove all fuel and purchased power costs from base

11        rates, the calculations may not include all the details would have been necessary to

12        develop an accurate base cost of fuel rate.

13

14   Q14. WHAT HAS THE COMMISSION REQUESTED IN PARAGRAPH 9.n OF

15        THE PRE-HEARING BENCH REQUEST?

16   A.   Paragraph 9.n of the Pre-Hearing Bench Request requests “A list of EPE regulatory

17        assets or other items currently being recovered through rate riders. An explanation

18        of whether those existing rate riders should be modified, terminated, or rolled into

19        the rate base.”

20


                                                8
                             EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY
                        SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
                                MANUEL CARRASCO


1    Q15. IN RESPONSE TO PARAGRAPH 9.n, PROVIDE A LIST OF EPE

2         REGULATORY ASSETS OR OTHER ITEMS CURRENTLY BEING

3         RECOVERED THROUGH RATE RIDERS.

 4   A.   EPE’s existing applicable riders/ rate adjustments include:

5            •    FPPCAC Rate No. 18,

 6           •    EUERF Rate No. 17,

 7           •    RPS Rider Rate No. 38,

 8           •    AMS Rider Rate No. 46,

 9           •    TEP Rider Rate No. 44, and

10           •    New Mexico Community Solar Administrative Cost Rider Rate No. 47.1.

11

12   Q16. IN FURTHER RESPONSE TO PARAGRAPH 9.n, PROVIDE AN

13        EXPLANATION OF WHETHER THOSE EXISTING RATE RIDERS

14        SHOULD BE MODIFIED, TERMINATED, OR ROLLED INTO THE RATE

15        BASE.

16   A.   EPE proposes to roll AMS Rider Rate No. 46 costs into base rates in this

17        proceeding, while maintaining that rate rider for costs incurred after the September

18        2025 Test Year Period. This is explained in the Direct Testimony of EPE witness

19        George Novela at pages 27-29.

20                EPE proposes that the remaining riders should be maintained. Specifically,


                                               9
                    EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY
               SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
                       MANUEL CARRASCO


 1   •   The FPPCAC Rate No. 18 will continue to function as a flow-through

 2       mechanism to recover variable fuel and purchased power costs, which are

 3       not appropriate for recovery through base rates due to their volatility.

 4   •   The EUERF Rate No. 17 will remain in place to recover approved energy

 5       efficiency program costs to support ongoing programs consistent with

 6       Commission directives.

 7   •   The RPS Rider Rate No. 38 will continue to facilitate recovery of the

 8       approved costs associated with compliance with Renewable Portfolio

 9       Standard requirements. However, in this proceeding, EPE proposes to move

10       into base rates the Commission approved annual capacity costs related to

11       the Santa Teresa Project Energy Storage Agreement (“ESA”) and the

12       capacity costs related to the Carne ESA. The Direct Testimony of EPE

13       witness Novela at pages 23-24 provides additional discussion including

14       EPE’s intent to also move energy costs incurred under Commission

15       approved PPAs out of the RPS Cost Rider and into its Fuel and Purchase

16       Power Cost Adjustment Clause, pending Commission approval in EPE’s

17       2026 REA Plan Case.

18   •   The TEP Rider Rate No. 44 will continue to provide recovery of costs

19       associated with EPE’s Transportation Electrification Plan, including

20       approved investments and program-related expenditures.


                                       10
                            EL PASO ELECTRIC COMPANY
                       SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT TESTIMONY OF
                               MANUEL CARRASCO


1           •   The New Mexico Community Solar Administrative Cost Rider Rate No.

2               47.1 will remain in place to recover administrative costs associated with

3               implementation and operation of the community solar program.

4        Accordingly, no additional modifications or terminations to EPE’s riders are

5        proposed at this time.

6

7   Q17. DOES      THIS      CONCLUDE        YOUR       SUPPLEMENTAL           DIRECT

8        TESTIMONY?

9   A.   Yes.

  DECLARATION OF MANUEL CARRASCO IN SUPPORT OF THE FOREGOING
 SUPPLEMENTAL DIRECT TESTIMONY TO THE COMMISSION’S APRIL 23, 2026
                  PRE-HEARING BENCH REQUEST

       I, Manuel Carrasco, pursuant to Rule 1-011 NMRA, state as follows:

       1.     I affirm in writing under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of

New Mexico that the following statements are true and correct.

       2.     I am over 18 years of age and have personal knowledge of the facts stated herein.

I am employed by El Paso Electric Company ("EPE" or “the Company”) as the Manager – Rate

Research.

       3.     The foregoing Supplemental Direct Testimony of Manuel Carrasco, together with

all exhibits sponsored therein and attached thereto, is true and accurate based on my knowledge

and belief.

       4.     I submit this Declaration, based upon my personal knowledge and upon information

and belief, in support of EPE Application for Revisions of Its Retail Electric Rates Pursuant to

Advice Notice No. 317.
